description: Machine-readable live work queue. Passing entries are retained for 24 hours, then removed by pnpm features:prune; durable behavior and evidence remain in product specs and Git/PR history. See docs/FEATURES.md for rules.

features.behavior: DataGrip-style grid editing: single-click whole-cell selection; double-click/Enter/F2 inline editing for scalar values; shared True/False boolean and enum selectors; lossless date, time, time-with-time-zone, timestamp, and PostgreSQL interval editing; automatic dismissal of any active scalar, structured, or inserted-row editor when another body cell is clicked; compact right-side drawer editing for JSON, supported arrays, binary hex, XML, and intervals, with visible Format/Minify/Copy and fixed actions; grouped binary hex with byte count and ASCII preview under a friendly bytes label; plain-text JSON/array substring filters on SQL engines and native structured containment on MongoDB; validated PostgreSQL bit-string and network editing; anchored SET editing with optional full-panel expansion; spreadsheet keyboard navigation, typed copy/paste, nullable clearing, undo, staged dirty-state feedback, and page-level commit; automatic catalog/row refresh after successful SQL writes; fixed-width truncated columns; adaptive icon-only shell tabs and row actions below the desktop breakpoint; and a non-executing SQL Explain action with no Analyze control.

features.evidence: Draft PR #160 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/160), round 8 pushed as bdf2667, round 9 as c74d70a, and round 10 implemented as 148d4b7. Rounds 3-10 live-review refinements: true whole-cell selection/edit ring; borderless scalar input; shared True/False and enum selectors; nullable clearing without a NULL chip; plain URL display; deterministic long-text truncation whose column width remains stable in edit mode; centered loading states; adaptive labels below 1024px; every grid editor dismisses on a different body-cell click; lossless temporal and PostgreSQL interval editing, including legacy parsed interval objects; SQL Analyze UI removed and Explain always non-executing; compact right-side editing for JSON, supported arrays, bytea/blob/BLOB hex, XML, and interval values; restored JSON Format/Minify/Copy; grouped binary hex with byte count and ASCII preview; disabled Apply for invalid drawer drafts; validated PostgreSQL bit/bit varying and network text; plain-text structured substring filters for PostgreSQL JSON/arrays, MySQL JSON, and SQLite JSON while MongoDB retains native structured containment; and immediate catalog/row refresh after successful non-read SQL. Focused component, core/server, driver unit/live integration, and PostgreSQL browser E2E suites pass. Browser QA confirms stable long-text width, compact drawer actions, ordinary `data` JSON filtering, readable interval text, and invalid-to-valid interval/bytes Apply states. Local `pnpm verify:pr` passes on Node 22 with 34/34 package tasks, check:state, smoke E2E (11 passed, 4 skipped), and full E2E (30 passed, 47 skipped) across PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, and MongoDB. Both GitHub jobs fail before any steps because the repository's Actions credits are exhausted.

features.behavior: Provide one compact, accessible control and typed-editor system for Qyre's write workflows: shared Button, IconButton, Field, Select/Combobox, and editor actions; lossless text, multiline, exact numeric/decimal, identifier, tri-state boolean, enum/set, date/time/timestamp, JSON/JSONB, supported-array, and MongoDB Extended JSON editors; explicit validation and before/after feedback; and explained read-only treatment for binary and unknown values. Preserve authoritative permission, --read-only, server-validation, driver, and transaction behavior across PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, and MongoDB.

features.behavior: Protect SQL row-editing integrity and make scalar activation predictable: define a mutation-specific editor capability matrix; fail closed for time and timestamp values until a lossless editor is verified; keep exact temporal values display-only; make row-background clicks select while editable cell controls activate consistently by pointer, Enter, or F2; and keep scalar editors overlaid so activating them does not resize rows or columns. Preserve permission, --read-only, transaction, and cross-engine behavior; MongoDB remains on its document editor.

features.behavior: Audit Qyre's complete web experience before changing production code: exercise first-use and returning-user flows, all four engines, writable/read-only/restricted sessions, dense data, destructive and recovery states, keyboard/accessibility behavior, light/dark themes, and responsive desktop widths; record evidence-backed findings, systemic causes, and an approval-gated product-wide polish plan with bounded implementation slices and acceptance criteria.
features.evidence: Draft PR #157 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/157), pushed as c24b1b3. Completed a live, evidence-backed audit across all four engines, writable/read-only/restricted sessions, both themes, dense and failure states, and 320-1440px widths; captured 35 screenshots and recorded 23 findings. User review triggered a deeper editing audit that confirmed conflicting selection/edit gestures, unstable Add/Commit UI, missing structured editors and shared controls, redundant writable status, and a critical minute-only temporal mutation fidelity risk. The user approved the revised nine-slice plan. Verified with pnpm verify:pr locally and through pre-push (34/34 package tasks, 11 smoke E2E passed/4 expected skips, 29 full E2E passed/43 expected skips); both GitHub CI jobs passed.

features.behavior: Close SUGGESTIONS.md U6: SchemaTab hardcodes targetSchema = schemas[0], so on multi-schema Postgres databases 'New table' silently creates in whichever schema sorts first with no way to choose. Add a schema selector to CreateTableDialog (defaulting sensibly, e.g. to the sidebar's current selection when set), thread the choice through useCreateTable to POST /api/schemas/:schema/tables.
features.evidence: Draft PR #153 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/153), pushed as 56ac0b9. Closed SUGGESTIONS.md U6 by adding a controlled SQL schema selector to CreateTableDialog. SchemaTab seeds it from the current sidebar table's schema when that schema is available, otherwise from the first introspected schema, and useCreateTable now carries the chosen schema in each mutation to POST /api/schemas/:schema/tables. MongoDB's collection dialog remains unchanged. Added UI coverage for the default and selectable schema list plus a web API test proving the selected schema owns the request route. Verified on Node 22 with @qyre/ui 366/366, @qyre/web 140/140, pnpm check:quiet 34/34, local and pre-push pnpm verify:pr (11 smoke E2E passed/4 skipped; 29 full E2E passed/43 skipped), and both GitHub CI jobs passed. The first push attempt hit the repository's documented transient Postgres autocomplete /api/tables timeout; its normal retry passed the complete gate.

features.behavior: Scalable-structure refactor across the ENTIRE workspace (every package and app; product source only, never test files), behavior-preserving - no functional changes. (1) Split every non-test source file over 500 lines into cohesive modules within a folder; as of 2026-07-14 that is packages/ui/src/data-grid/rows-table.tsx (933: extract toolbar, selection/drag logic, and row/cell rendering), packages/server/src/routes/schema-ddl.ts (640: split table-lifecycle, column, and index route groups), packages/ui/src/schema/table-structure.tsx (546: extract columns section, indexes section, table-actions section), and packages/ui/src/data-grid/filter-bar.tsx (517: extract filter-editor pieces) - but re-measure at execution time and split anything else that has crossed 500 lines since. (2) Group every flat folder that has grown past comfortable scanning into related subfolders, applied across the whole workspace (apps/web, packages/ui, packages/server, packages/cli, packages/core, packages/drivers/*, packages/config, packages/testing*): e.g. packages/server/src/routes (13 files) and src/services (14) by domain (rows/ddl/admin/import-export/infra), packages/ui/src/data-grid (11) and src/schema (9) by concern, and each packages/drivers/*/src (12-16 files) into introspection/mutation/admin groupings kept consistent across engines - plus any other folder found at execution time to exceed ~8 flat files. Respect docs/CODE_ORGANIZATION.md and ARCHITECTURE.md layer rules; keep each package's public exports (its index) unchanged so no consumer import breaks; pure moves/renames plus mechanical extraction only. Update docs/CODE_ORGANIZATION.md if the new folder conventions change what it documents.
features.evidence: Draft PR #154 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/154), pushed as 747e625. Reorganized production source across apps/web, packages/ui, packages/server, packages/core, packages/drivers/contract, and all four engine drivers into cohesive responsibility folders while preserving package public exports and leaving every test file in place. Split the four production files over 500 lines: RowsTable into table state, toolbar, footer, export, and types modules; FilterBar into filter-editor pieces; TableStructure into row renderers; and the schema DDL route into table, column, index, and shared-support groups. Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, and MongoDB were covered by the repository gate.

features.behavior: Eliminate Playwright fixture contention without discarding cross-engine parallelism. Add an automatic E2E fixture lock that serializes each test for every underlying engine fixture it touches (including read-only/restricted projects that share the writable engine database), lets different engines continue in parallel, acquires multi-engine locks in a stable order, and safely recovers locks left by dead worker processes. Route every Playwright spec through the fixture and explicitly declare the cross-engine Postgres-to-MongoDB journey. Add focused lock/mapping tests, remove the resolved reliability debt, and document the enforced isolation contract.

Multi-engine journeys acquire sorted locks, dead-worker locks are reclaimed, all 12 E2E specs use the shared fixture, and the resolved reliability debt was removed and documented. Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, and MongoDB fixture mappings and live suites were covered.
